questions.question: Which AWS service is the usual storage layer of a data lake?
questions.explanation: S3 is object storage: virtually unlimited, cheap, durable, and readable by Spark, Athena, Glue and others. EBS is a block disk attached to one instance; RDS is a managed relational database.

questions.question: Which Google Cloud service is a serverless data warehouse queried in SQL?
questions.explanation: BigQuery separates storage and compute, and you pay for storage and the data scanned (or for reserved capacity). Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL store, Cloud SQL is managed MySQL, PostgreSQL or SQL Server, and Dataproc is managed Spark/Hadoop.

questions.question: Which AWS service runs SQL directly on files in S3, without loading them into a database?
questions.explanation: Athena reads the files in place, using table definitions from the Glue Data Catalog, and by default bills by data scanned (provisioned capacity is an option). Partitioning and Parquet reduce both cost and latency.

questions.question: Why is AWS Lambda a poor fit for a 2-hour data transformation?
options: A Lambda invocation can run for 15 minutes at most
questions.explanation: Lambda is designed for short, event-driven tasks (up to 15 minutes). Long jobs belong on containers (ECS/Fargate, Cloud Run jobs), managed Spark (EMR, Dataproc, Glue) or a batch service.

questions.question: A function running in AWS needs to read one S3 bucket. What is the right way to grant access?
options: Put an admin user's access keys in its environment variables
Attach an IAM role that allows read access to that bucket only
questions.explanation: Least privilege: grant only what is needed, through a role that provides short-lived credentials automatically. Long-lived keys stored in code or configuration are the most common source of leaks.

questions.question: Why deploy a production database across several Availability Zones?
options: To keep running if one data center (zone) fails
To make queries faster for users in other countries
questions.explanation: An Availability Zone is one or more isolated data centers within a region, with independent power and networking. Multi-AZ provides high availability with automatic failover; serving users in other countries is what multi-region setups are for.

questions.question: Logs must be kept for 7 years for compliance and are almost never read. Which storage is the cheapest fit?
questions.explanation: Archive tiers cost far less per GB but take hours to restore, which is acceptable for compliance data. Lifecycle rules can move objects there automatically after N days.

questions.question: Which practices reduce the cost of a cloud data platform? Select all that apply.
options: Partitioned, columnar files so queries scan less data
Lifecycle policies that move old data to colder storage
Autoscaling, and shutting down idle clusters
questions.explanation: Scan-based pricing (Athena, BigQuery on demand) rewards Parquet and partitioning. Storage tiers and turning compute off when idle are the other big levers. Uncompressed CSV increases both storage and scan costs.

questions.question: Order the steps of an event-driven ingestion of a daily file on AWS.
steps: The partner uploads the file to an S3 landing prefix
An S3 event notification triggers a Lambda function
The function validates the file and writes it as Parquet to a partitioned path
The new partition is registered in the Glue Data Catalog
Analysts query it in SQL with Athena
questions.explanation: No server runs while waiting: each step is triggered by the previous one. Keeping the original file in the landing prefix makes reprocessing possible.

questions.question: Order the steps of giving a new pipeline least-privilege access on AWS.
steps: List the exact resources and actions the pipeline needs
Write an IAM policy limited to them
Attach the policy to a role for the pipeline's compute
The pipeline assumes the role and gets short-lived credentials
Review the access logs (CloudTrail) and tighten the policy over time
questions.explanation: Roles avoid long-lived keys entirely. Starting narrow and widening only when needed is safer than starting broad and hoping to restrict later.
